task: A strategically located border city that serves as the primary gateway for trade between two rival powers has petitioned for expanded self-governance. The city's merchant council argues that its unique position requires flexibility in tariffs, legal codes, and diplomatic representation that a distant central government cannot provide. Granting autonomy would likely increase trade revenue and reduce administrative burden, but it would also create a precedent that other prosperous cities might follow, potentially eroding central authority. The rival power has signalled that it would view the city's autonomy as an opportunity to expand its own influence there. Design a governance framework for the border city that grants sufficient flexibility to maximise its economic function while preserving its political loyalty and preventing foreign co-option.

dispatches.responsibility: Draft the border-city charter, the bounded tariff schedule (numeric ceilings and floors for transit duties, market fees, and foreign-currency exchange), the merchant-council remit, and the sunset/renewal mechanism for the autonomy grant; specify the data the council must report to the central government each season

Design the central garrison deployment, the chain of command that keeps the city watch under central command (numeric cap on locally recruited guards, foreign-born guard ban), and the rules for any local militia; define the threshold at which unrest or foreign troop movement on the border triggers central reinforcement

Design the commercial court system: which categories of cases (trade disputes, customs fraud, foreign merchant status) the city court can finally decide, which must be appealed or referred to the central court, the oath/registration regime for city judges, and the cooling-off rules for judges sitting on cases involving the rival power

Design the censorate audit cycle, the list of automatic tripwire reviews (debt ratio, land transfer to foreigners, fortifications, foreign debt, militia expansion, diplomatic correspondence), the escalation channel to the central government when thresholds trip, and the powers of the central magistrate to suspend local acts pending review
